spec_family.name: New Construction Cabinet Painting
spec_family.description: Combined prime+paint spec for residential new construction on-site cabinet finishing — kitchen, bathroom, laundry, and utility cabinets. Covers box exteriors, face frames, doors, drawers, and optionally cabinet interiors. Doors and drawer fronts are removed, painted flat on sawhorses, cured 5-7 days minimum, then reinstalled (separate mobilization). Box/frame work is done in-place. 4 paintable items: ITM_CABINET_DOOR (EA), ITM_CABINET_DRAWER (EA), ITM_CABINET_FRAME (SF), ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR (SF conditional on scope=full_with_interior). Substrate-driven primer selection for bare substrates; primer conditional on substrate_state. QT-driven finish systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Cabinet interiors always QT3 regardless of exterior tier (AWI semi-exposed standard). 9 protection zones including countertop, backsplash, and appliance coverage unique to kitchen/bath environments. 5 modifiers: door_style, quality_tier, height, kitchen_complexity, masking_scope (informational). Material systems are QT-driven recommendations — contractor retains discretion.

includes: Kitchen cabinets (upper, lower, pantry, island)
Bathroom vanity cabinets
Laundry room and utility cabinets
Mudroom cabinets (cabinet-style construction with doors/drawers)
Cabinet doors — all styles: slab, shaker, raised panel, glass frame (frame only, glass excluded)
Cabinet drawer front faces
Face frames (stiles, rails)
End panels and exposed box surfaces
Toe kicks and filler strips
Light valances and decorative trim pieces
Crown molding integral to cabinet tops
Hardware removal (hinges, pulls, knobs, catches), bag, label, reinstall after cure
Door and drawer removal, label, flat painting on sawhorses, reinstallation after 5-7 day cure
MDF edge sealing with shellac (bare MDF only — step 1 of two-step prime)
Surface prep per substrate type (fill, caulk, sand, clean)
Primer coat — conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE (substrate-driven chemistry)
Finish coat application (spray or brush) — 2 coats standard, 3+ at QT5 brush per FFD SS15.10.3
Between-coat interstage process (inspect, sand, repair, clean) at ALL quality tiers
Floor protection (full kitchen for spray, perimeter for brush)
Countertop protection (kraft/rosin paper + plastic for spray)
Backsplash masking
Wall and ceiling masking (spray method only)
Appliance masking (if present — atypical for NC)
Plumbing and electrical masking
Cabinet interior painting (conditional on scope=full_with_interior, always QT3, spray-only)
Final quality inspection
Protection teardown and cleanup

excludes.item: Built-in bookshelves, entertainment centers, mudroom cubbies (open shelving)
Plumbing disconnect for sink base (GC responsibility)
Drawer box interiors (functional surfaces, not cosmetic)

excludes.route_to: Not fixed cabinetry — not in scope

excludes.item: Thermofoil / melamine cabinets (factory-finished, not suitable for on-site painting)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, repair scope, material system, and coat count.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3 standard residential. QT4 premium — waterborne alkyd recommended per FFD. QT5 showroom — premium product mandatory, spray strongly preferred. Cabinet interiors always QT3 regardless of exterior tier (AWI semi-exposed standard).

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for primer and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray strongly preferred per Fine Finish Doctrine SS10.3 and SS15.1.2. Brush method uses Roll and Tip technique per SS15.6. Cabinet interiors are spray-only in practice (access constraints). Brush method adds 1.4x time modifier. No roll — 'brush' here means brush/roll using Roll and Tip methodology.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish sheen. Constrained by quality tier gate.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Semi-gloss is kitchen/bath standard for cleanability. Gloss requires QT5 + spray method.

configuration_dimensions.description: Input substrate condition. Drives primer requirement and prep scope.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_BARE: full primer coat required (substrate-driven chemistry, MDF two-step edge seal). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer — factory-primed is common NC delivery. Per Doctrine SS2.1: primer on factory-primed is optional (user decision).

configuration_dimensions.description: Cabinet painting scope — which item groups are active.
configuration_dimensions.notes: doors_only = ITM_CABINET_DOOR + ITM_CABINET_DRAWER only (frame already finished or not in scope). full_exterior = doors + drawers + frame + end panels + toe kick. full_with_interior = full exterior + ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR. Scope controls which items are active in the variant.

paintable_items.name: Cabinet door face
paintable_items.counting_rules: Each door face counted individually. Removed from cabinet, painted flat on sawhorses/pyramids. Style complexity (slab, shaker, raised_panel, glass_frame) handled by door_style modifier. Both faces counted separately if scope includes interior.
paintable_items.notes: New item. Distinct from ITM_BUILTIN_DOOR (built-in millwork doors) and door slab items (ITM_DOOR_SLAB). Glass doors excluded — not painted.

paintable_items.name: Cabinet drawer front face
paintable_items.counting_rules: Each drawer front face counted individually. Removed from cabinet, painted flat on sawhorses. Drawer box interior NOT painted (functional surface, not cosmetic). Style follows door_style modifier.
paintable_items.notes: New item. ~0.7x door time per unit (smaller surface area, same technique). Large pot drawers approach door size.

paintable_items.name: Cabinet face frame and exposed box surfaces
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total SF of paintable face frame and exposed box surfaces: stiles, rails, end panels, toe kicks, filler strips, light valances. Painted in-place after doors/drawers removed. PaintScope provides direct SF measurement.
paintable_items.notes: New item. Includes all exposed box surfaces. Height modifier applies for upper cabinets in tall rooms. Kitchen_complexity modifier applies.

paintable_items.name: Cabinet box interior surfaces
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total SF of cabinet interior surfaces — inside walls, ceiling, floor of cabinet box, fixed shelves. Spray-only in practice. Always QT3 regardless of exterior tier (AWI semi-exposed standard).
paintable_items.notes: New item. Separate line item for independent pricing and optional inclusion. Interior spray is awkward due to access constraints.

variants.notes: Common NC scenario. Factory-primed, standard spray. Builder-grade kitchen.
Premium kitchen spray. Waterborne alkyd (SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE) recommended.
Showroom spray. QT5 spray still uses 2 finish coats (3 coats is QT5+brush only).
Factory-primed, standard brush. Minimal room masking — no ceiling/wall/appliance.
Premium brush. Waterborne alkyd STRONGLY recommended for open time.
Factory-primed, showroom brush. 3 finish coats per FFD SS15.10.3. NOTE: QT5+gloss+brush is NOT RECOMMENDED — spray preferred.
Bare substrate, standard spray. Full primer workflow including MDF edge seal if applicable.
Bare substrate, premium spray. Bonding primer recommended at QT4+.
Bare substrate, showroom brush. 4 total coats (1P + 3F), 3 interstage cycles. Slowest variant. NOT RECOMMENDED — spray preferred.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of cabinet door faces to be painted. Each face counted separately.
Count of cabinet drawer front faces to be painted.
Total SF of face frame and exposed box surfaces (stiles, rails, end panels, toe kicks, filler strips).
Total SF of cabinet interior surfaces.
Total hardware piece count (hinges + pulls + knobs) for removal/reinstall labor.
Total LF of cabinet-to-wall caulk joints (sides, top, crown, filler strips, toe kick).
Room count for setup/cleanup and FIXED-time tasks.
Floor area requiring protection in cabinet work zone.
Perimeter floor protection for brush method.
Countertop surface area requiring protection. High-value surfaces — kraft paper + plastic for spray.
Linear footage of backsplash requiring masking.
Wall area requiring masking for spray overspray protection.
Ceiling area requiring masking for spray overspray protection.
Number of appliances requiring masking. Atypical for NC.

protection_zones_required.notes: Full kitchen floor coverage for cabinet spray work. Canvas drop cloths + tape edges. High-value flooring (hardwood, tile).
Drop cloth runners at cabinet base. Brush drip and sanding dust protection only.
CRITICAL: high-value surfaces (granite, quartz, marble). Kraft/rosin paper + plastic sheeting for spray. Paper + tape for brush. Paint drips on stone can cause permanent damage.
Tile backsplash masking between counter and upper cabinets. Green tape edge seal against tile for clean line.
Plastic sheeting on walls for spray overspray. Full wall coverage. Spray only.
Ceiling fixtures, under-cabinet lighting near spray work area. Includes ceiling masking (plastic sheeting) for spray method.
Full appliance wrap — plastic sheeting + tape. Conditional on appliances being present (atypical for NC). Spray only.
Cabinet hardware removed, bagged, and labeled — not masked in place. Remove hinges, pulls, knobs, catches, soft-close mechanisms.
Plumbing fixtures in sink base cabinet (pipes, valves). Electrical: switch plates/outlet covers removed and bagged. Under-cabinet lighting masked.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Cabinet frame meets wall at sides and top. Different finish — cabinet enamel vs wall paint. Caulk seals gap during prep.
Upper cabinet tops may approach ceiling in standard-height rooms. Crown molding bridges gap if integral to cabinet.
Door overlays face frame. Same finish. Doors removed during painting — no edge conflict during application.
Face frame edge meets interior. Interior typically QT3 vs exterior QT (may differ). Interior painted through door openings after doors removed.

valid_input_states.notes: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE requires full primer workflow (substrate-driven chemistry). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer — standard NC delivery. MDF substrates in SS_BARE state require shellac edge seal BEFORE latex face primer.

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished wall needs no protection from brush. Spray still creates overspray — but unpainted drywall is easily covered by subsequent wall painting.
Finished walls need full masking during cabinet spray work.
Brush application has no overspray risk. Cabinet-to-wall junction caulked.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when floor is subfloor.
site_condition_rules.notes: Kitchen floors are commonly finished (hardwood, tile, LVP) even in NC by the time cabinets are painted.

site_condition_rules.effect: Temperature affects dry times, cure times, and application quality. Cold extends cure period significantly. Hot causes flash drying.
site_condition_rules.notes: Refer to manufacturer PDS for temperature limits. HVAC should be operational for cabinet painting.

site_condition_rules.effect: MDF edge sealing uses solvent-based products — adequate ventilation required. Spray generates overspray requiring air exchange.
site_condition_rules.notes: Kitchen ventilation is typically adequate with range hood and windows. Isolate from HVAC to prevent dust circulation.

site_condition_rules.effect: Construction dust is the primary quality enemy for cabinet finishing. HEPA vacuum, tack cloth, seal HVAC vents, isolate work zone with zippered barriers.
site_condition_rules.notes: Schedule cabinet painting AFTER dusty trades complete. Cabinet work is ideally the last interior painting scope.

site_condition_rules.effect: Height modifier via ceiling height: standard_8ft=1.0x, tall_9_10ft=1.15x, extra_tall_11_12ft=1.30x.
site_condition_rules.notes: Upper cabinets in tall kitchens require step ladder or scaffold. Door/drawer tasks unaffected (painted at ground level).

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Cabinet painting is typically the last interior painting scope in NC. Schedule AFTER drywall/trim/wall painting to minimize dust contamination on wet cabinet finishes. Same crew handles all millwork painting (cabinets, trim, doors).
sequencing_notes.internal_sequence: Protection setup > Hardware remove > Door/drawer remove > Prep (fill, caulk, sand, MDF edge seal, clean) > [Prime if bare] > Interstage > Finish coat 1 > Interstage > Finish coat 2 > [QT5 brush: Interstage > Coat 3] > Final inspect > 5-7 DAY CURE PERIOD > Reinstall hardware > Reinstall doors/drawers > Alignment touchup > Remove protection > Cleanup.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Floor > Countertop > Backsplash > Wall masking (spray) > Ceiling masking (spray) > Appliance masking (spray) > Plumbing masking > Electrical masking > Work coats > Teardown in reverse > Vacuum.
sequencing_notes.door_workflow: Remove doors/drawers (SETUP) > Label and bag hardware > Paint flat on sawhorses (horizontal orientation) > 5-7 day cure (SEPARATE MOBILIZATION) > Reinstall doors > Reinstall drawers > Reinstall hardware > Adjust alignment > Verify soft-close operation > Touch-up handling damage.
sequencing_notes.two_mobilization_note: Cabinet painting requires TWO separate site visits: (1) setup/prep/prime/finish/inspect, (2) return after 5-7 day cure for reinstall/touchup/cleanup. This is a scheduling constraint, not a rate adjustment.

relationships.notes: Cabinet painting is typically the LAST interior painting scope — after walls, ceilings, and trim. Minimizes dust contamination on wet cabinet finishes. Shares Fine Finish material systems with all millwork specs. Scope boundary with SF_BUILTIN_NC: cabinets with doors/drawers → SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT; open shelving/built-ins → SF_BUILTIN_NC.

inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: No dry times in specs — refer to product PDS.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Material system selection is mandatory doctrine
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Material systems are suggestions per QT — contractor has discretion.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC cabinet painting (Spec #18). Key features: 4 paintable items (ITM_CABINET_DOOR EA, ITM_CABINET_DRAWER EA, ITM_CABINET_FRAME SF, ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR SF conditional), 5 configuration dimensions (quality_tier, application_method, sheen, substrate_state, scope), 9 protection zones (countertop, backsplash, floor, wall, ceiling, appliance, plumbing, electrical, hardware — more than any prior spec), 5 modifiers (door_style, quality_tier, height, kitchen_complexity, masking_scope), door/drawer removal + flat painting + 5-7 day cure + reinstall (two mobilizations), MDF two-step edge seal, AWI semi-exposed standard for interiors (always QT3), 58 SOP tasks across 7 modules (33 binary + 25 qt_scaled), 4 round configurations, 9 variants. 10 material systems (7 primer + 3 finish, 1 new SYS_PRIMER_BONDING proposed). QA: pass_with_warnings (0 critical, 2 major fixed, 6 minor non-blocking).
